answer: Each agent claims one vertex on the plume registry and posts a 70-credit bond keyed to it. At dawn the agent files a signed plume sample: vertex coordinates and concentration. An auditor recomputes the concentration from the source table and dawn wind log; a mismatch or a reused or copied seal burns the bond. The first filing costs 37, the kth pays 37+4(k-1), so the 1000th pays 4033 and 1000 fakes pay 2,035,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-vertex ring fails because a rented seal cannot sign a dawn sample for its own key. An honest agent pays 37 once and reclaims the bond after audit.
